# memoire

> SQLite databases on demand for agents, shared across teams and machines. Open source (Apache-2.0, Rust). Early: v1 is in progress. The hosted service at https://app.memoire.network is invite-only for now.

One always-on gateway handles every request, and the SQLite files live on its host. Agents and people create databases with the `memoire` CLI and query them over an HTTP JSON API.

- Burstable databases are scratch space. They expire after an idle TTL (24 hours by default, at most 7 days after creation) and have no backups.
- Persistent databases live until deleted. They are snapshotted every 6 hours, and snapshots are kept 7 days.
- Access is per team. Members sign in. Machines and agents use API keys (`mzk_…`) that can be narrowed, for example to read-only.
- Limits: 1 GiB per database, 50 active databases per team.

## Get started

From nothing to a signed-in CLI. The hosted service at https://app.memoire.network is invite-only for now, so a person needs an invitation to get an account. Self-hosting is in the [deployment guide](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/docs/deploy/dokploy.md).

Steps 2 and 3 need a person in a browser. An agent that already has a key starts at step 4, or uses the two variables in step 6.

1. Install the CLI. There are no release binaries yet, so Cargo builds the CLI from source. That needs Rust 1.98 or later. The binary is `memoire`.

   ```sh
   cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire memoire-cli
   ```

2. Open https://app.memoire.network, sign in and create a team. Databases, machines and keys belong to it.

3. Create a key for this machine. In the web app, open "Machines and API keys" and add a machine. The app then offers a key for it. Pick read-only access if the machine only needs to read. The app shows the key (`mzk_…`) once, so copy it now.

4. Sign the CLI in. `login` asks for the key and does not echo it. Paste it at the prompt. The CLI checks the key with the service, then stores it in `~/.config/memoire/credentials.json` with mode 0600. Without a terminal, `login` reads the key from standard input or from `--key-file FILE`. Never pass a key as an argument.

   ```sh
   memoire login --server https://app.memoire.network
   ```

   Then check who the CLI is signed in as.

   ```sh
   memoire whoami
   ```

5. Teach your agents (optional). This installs the memoire skill, which teaches Claude Code and Codex the commands. It needs no login.

   ```sh
   memoire skill install --claude --codex
   ```

6. Agents and CI. An agent or a CI job skips `login` and reads two variables: `MEMOIRE_SERVER=https://app.memoire.network` and `MEMOIRE_API_KEY`, the machine's key from your secret store. Give each machine its own key.

   Once signed in, a team owner or admin can mint those keys from the CLI. It asks for the person's email and password without echo and prints only the key, so the key goes straight to a file and never into an argument. The `umask` keeps that file readable by you alone.

   ```sh
   (umask 077 && memoire keys create --name ci-runner > ci-runner.key)
   ```

   Move the file to the new machine, store the key and remove the file.

   ```sh
   memoire login --server https://app.memoire.network --key-file ci-runner.key && rm ci-runner.key
   ```

## Benchmarks

Measured on 21 November 2026 against the hosted service by one Python client about 3 ms away, on one burstable database of 1.4 million rows. Latencies are client-side, so they include the network round trip. The server and the client were both shared with other work, so read them as an order of magnitude.

- Round trip alone (`GET /health/live`): p50 2.8 ms, p99 18 ms.
- Read one row by primary key: p50 13.0 ms, p95 30.5 ms, p99 55.6 ms. A 1,000-row page: p50 14.1 ms. Insert one row: p50 13.3 ms, p99 79.5 ms.
- A small request costs about 13 ms whatever it reads or writes. About 12 ms of that is the round trip, the credential check and finding the database, and 1 to 2 ms is SQLite.
- A new connection adds 16 to 20 ms of TCP and TLS, so keep connections open.
- A join and group over 100,000 orders and their 300,000 items: 1.8 s. With four times the data: 13.6 s, past the 5 s default deadline.
- Loading over HTTP: 48,000 to 77,000 rows/s. Generating rows inside SQLite: 465,000 to 609,000 rows/s.
- Limits in force: 100 statements per request, 999 parameters per statement, 1 MiB per request body, 10,000 rows per statement and 16 MiB per response, 5 s per statement by default and 30 s at most, 1 GiB per database.
- Not measured: capacity with many clients or databases, a database's first request after 5 minutes idle, persistent databases and snapshots, import, the memory routes.

The method, every number and the raw results are in the [benchmarks](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md). [`scripts/bench.py`](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/scripts/bench.py) runs them again.

## Documentation

- [Repository](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire): source, README and status
- [CLI](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/docs/cli.md): every `memoire` command, its output and exit codes
- [HTTP API](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/docs/api.md): the contract between the gateway and its clients
- [Architecture](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): contexts, data plane rules and limits
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md): measured latency and throughput of the hosted service, the method, the limits and what the numbers do not show
- [Agent memory](https://github.com/ligerian-labs/memoire/blob/main/docs/memory.md): `memoire memory` keeps a shared memory for a fleet of agents in a memoire database; agents recall, record, confirm and dispute what they verified
